subproblem.title: Positive mass in every ball about 0 forces one of finitely many parallel planes through 0
subproblem.statement: Let P, n, N ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace (of any dimension), let w_1, …, w_N ∈ V^⊥ (w : Fin N → ℝ^P), let α_1, …, α_N ∈ ℝ be arbitrary, and let ν = Σ_{i} ofReal(α_i)·Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w_i ∈ V} (a finite sum of measures over Fin N; Hⁿ = μHE[n]; ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal). If ν(B_r(0)) > 0 for every r > 0 (open balls), then w_i = 0 for some i.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (N : ℕ) (w : Fin N → Euclid P) (α : Fin N → ℝ), (∀ i, w i ∈ Vᗮ) → ν = ∑ i, ENNReal.ofReal (α i) • (μHE[n]).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - w i ∈ V} → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → 0 < ν (ball 0 r)) → ∃ i, w i = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 ("Some w_i = 0") of the selected proof, with the vanishing half of step 1 (a plane at distance ≥ r from 0 misses B_r(0)) proved inline. No dimension hypothesis, sign condition on the α_i or sibling lemma is needed.
Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n]; Π_i := {y : y − w_i ∈ V}; ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal (so ofReal(α_i) = 0 if α_i ≤ 0).
1. (Contradiction hypothesis.) Suppose w_i ≠ 0 for every i ∈ Fin N. Then ‖w_i‖ > 0 for every i (norm_pos_iff).
2. (A small radius.) There is r > 0 with r < ‖w_i‖ for every i. Indeed, for each i the condition r < ‖w_i‖ holds for all r in a neighbourhood of 0 (eventually_lt_nhds, as 0 < ‖w_i‖), hence eventually in the filter 𝓝[>]0; finitely many such conditions hold simultaneously eventually (Filter.eventually_all over the finite type Fin N); r > 0 holds eventually in 𝓝[>]0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin); and 𝓝[>]0 is a nontrivial filter, so some r satisfies all of them (Filter.Eventually.exists). (Concretely, for N ≥ 1, r := (min_i‖w_i‖)/2 works; for N = 0 any r > 0 works.)
3. (Each plane misses B_r(0).) Fix i and let y ∈ Π_i, i.e. t := y − w_i ∈ V. As w_i ∈ V^⊥, ⟨t, w_i⟩ = 0 (Submodule.inner_right_of_mem_orthogonal), and Pythagoras (norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_real, stated in Mathlib in the product form ‖t + w_i‖·‖t + w_i‖ = ‖t‖·‖t‖ + ‖w_i‖·‖w_i‖) with t + w_i = y gives ‖y‖² = ‖t‖² + ‖w_i‖² ≥ ‖w_i‖². Since 0 < r < ‖w_i‖, ‖w_i‖² > r², so ‖y‖² > r². If ‖y‖ < r held, then 0 ≤ ‖y‖ < r would give ‖y‖² < r², a contradiction; hence ‖y‖ ≥ r and y ∉ B_r(0). Thus B_r(0) ∩ Π_i = ∅ for every i.
4. (ν vanishes on B_r(0).) B_r(0) is open, hence measurable (measurableSet_ball). By the hypothesis on ν, the evaluation of a finite sum of measures (Measure.finsetSum_apply), Measure.smul_apply and Measure.restrict_apply (with the measurable set B_r(0)): ν(B_r(0)) = Σ_i ofReal(α_i)·Hⁿ(B_r(0) ∩ Π_i) = Σ_i ofReal(α_i)·Hⁿ(∅) = 0, by step 3.
5. (Conclusion.) Step 4 contradicts the hypothesis ν(B_r(0)) > 0 for the radius r > 0 of step 2. Hence w_i = 0 for some i. (For N = 0 the sum is empty, ν = 0, and the same contradiction shows the hypotheses are inconsistent, so the statement holds.) ∎
proof_key_steps: If every w_i ≠ 0, choose r > 0 with r < ‖w_i‖ for all i (finitely many positive numbers).
Pythagoras with w_i ∈ V^⊥ gives ‖y‖ ≥ ‖w_i‖ > r for y with y − w_i ∈ V, so every plane misses B_r(0).
Hence ν(B_r(0)) = Σ_i ofReal(α_i)·Hⁿ(∅) = 0, contradicting ν(B_r(0)) > 0; so some w_i = 0.

subproblem.title: Hⁿ of an offset parallel n-plane inside a ball centred at 0
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim V = n (Module.finrank ℝ V = n), let w ∈ V^⊥ and R ∈ ℝ with ‖w‖ < R. Then Hⁿ({y ∈ ℝ^P : y − w ∈ V} ∩ B_R(0)) = ω_n·ofReal((√(R² − ‖w‖²))ⁿ), where Hⁿ = μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P = Euclid P, B_R(0) is the open ball, ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝⁿ, and √ = Real.sqrt.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (w : Euclid P) (R : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → w ∈ Vᗮ → ‖w‖ < R → μHE[n] ({y : Euclid P | y - w ∈ V} ∩ ball 0 R) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (R ^ 2 - ‖w‖ ^ 2) ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 ("A plane in a ball") of the selected proof, case ‖w‖ < R. Uses the sibling subspace_ball (idtp_tdc_subspace_ball_measure): for a linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P with finrank ℝ Q = n, y ∈ Q and ρ > 0, Hⁿ(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ).
Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P = Euclid P; ω_n = unitBallVolume n; Π_w := {y : y − w ∈ V}; B_r(0) is the open ball.
1. (Radius.) Since 0 ≤ ‖w‖ < R, we have R > 0 and R² − ‖w‖² = (R − ‖w‖)(R + ‖w‖) > 0. Put ρ := √(R² − ‖w‖²) (Real.sqrt). Then ρ > 0 (Real.sqrt_pos) and ρ² = R² − ‖w‖² (Real.sq_sqrt).
2. (Pythagoras.) For every t ∈ V, w ∈ V^⊥ gives ⟨t, w⟩ = 0 (Submodule.inner_right_of_mem_orthogonal), hence ‖t + w‖² = ‖t‖² + ‖w‖² (norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_real, which Mathlib states in the product form ‖t + w‖·‖t + w‖ = ‖t‖·‖t‖ + ‖w‖·‖w‖; rewrite with sq or nlinarith).
3. (The translate.) Let T : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, T(t) := t + w. T is an isometry (translations are isometries; Mathlib isometry_add_right). We claim T(V ∩ B_ρ(0)) = Π_w ∩ B_R(0).
 (⊆) Let t ∈ V with ‖t‖ < ρ. Then T(t) − w = t ∈ V, so T(t) ∈ Π_w. As 0 ≤ ‖t‖ < ρ, ‖t‖² < ρ², so by step 2, ‖T(t)‖² = ‖t‖² + ‖w‖² < ρ² + ‖w‖² = R²; since R > 0 this gives ‖T(t)‖ < R, i.e. T(t) ∈ B_R(0).
 (⊇) Let y ∈ Π_w with ‖y‖ < R. Put t := y − w; then t ∈ V and T(t) = y. By step 2 applied to t (t + w = y), ‖y‖² = ‖t‖² + ‖w‖², so ‖t‖² = ‖y‖² − ‖w‖² < R² − ‖w‖² = ρ² (using 0 ≤ ‖y‖ < R); since ρ > 0 and ‖t‖ ≥ 0, ‖t‖ < ρ. Hence y = T(t) with t ∈ V ∩ B_ρ(0).
4. (Isometry invariance.) By Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image applied to the isometry T, Hⁿ(T(S)) = Hⁿ(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^P. With S := V ∩ B_ρ(0) and step 3: Hⁿ(Π_w ∩ B_R(0)) = Hⁿ(V ∩ B_ρ(0)).
5. (subspace_ball.) Apply subspace_ball with Q := V, centre y := 0 ∈ V (Submodule.zero_mem), radius ρ > 0 (step 1) and finrank ℝ V = n: Hⁿ(V ∩ B_ρ(0)) = ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ).
6. (Conclusion.) By steps 4 and 5, Hⁿ({y : y − w ∈ V} ∩ B_R(0)) = ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ) = ω_n·ofReal((√(R² − ‖w‖²))ⁿ). The argument is uniform in n, including n = 0 (V = {0}, Π_w = {w}). ∎
proof_key_steps: Since 0 ≤ ‖w‖ < R, ρ := √(R² − ‖w‖²) satisfies ρ > 0 and ρ² = R² − ‖w‖².
Pythagoras: ‖t + w‖² = ‖t‖² + ‖w‖² for t ∈ V, because w ∈ V^⊥.
The isometry t ↦ t + w maps V ∩ B_ρ(0) onto {y : y − w ∈ V} ∩ B_R(0).
Isometry invariance of μHE[n] and subspace_ball (centre 0 ∈ V, radius ρ) give ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ).

audit.reason: The prose matches the standalone Lean proposition. The norm bound implies positive R and square-root radius. Both translation-image containments follow from Pythagoras; isometry invariance and the declared subspace_ball dependency then give the exact formula. All hypotheses are used correctly, with no omitted case or circular reliance.

subproblem.title: Euclidean growth of a sum of weighted parallel n-planes bounds its total weight by 1
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim V = n (Module.finrank ℝ V = n), let Z ⊆ V^⊥ be any set and a : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] any function, and let ν = Σ_{w∈Z} a(w)·Hⁿ⌞{y : y − w ∈ V} (Measure.sum indexed by the subtype Z; Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Assume ν(B_R(0)) ≤ ω_n·ofReal(Rⁿ) for every R > 0 (B_R(0) the open ball, ω_n = unitBallVolume n). Then Σ'_{w∈Z} a(w) ≤ 1, the unconditional sum (tsum) over the subtype Z being taken in [0, ∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (Z : Set (Euclid P)) (a : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → Z ⊆ (Vᗮ : Set (Euclid P)) → ν = Measure.sum (fun w : Z => a w • (μHE[n]).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - w ∈ V}) → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ν (ball 0 R) ≤ unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (R ^ n)) → ∑' w : Z, a w ≤ 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 ("Evaluating ν") and 3 ("Finite subfamilies") of the selected proof, together with the bound Σ_{w∈Z}a(w) ≤ 1 of step 4, stated as a bound on the unconditional sum over Z. Uses the sibling plane_ball (cbr_ci_cp_fp_offset_plane_ball_measure): if finrank ℝ V = n, w ∈ V^⊥ and ‖w‖ < R, then Hⁿ({y : y − w ∈ V} ∩ B_R(0)) = ω_n·ofReal((√(R² − ‖w‖²))ⁿ).
Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n]; Π_z := {y : y − z ∈ V}; ω := ω_n = unitBallVolume n = volume(B_1(0) ⊆ Euclid n). Sums of [0, ∞]-valued terms are taken in [0, ∞]; nothing is assumed about countability of Z, measurability of a, or finiteness of the values a(z).
1. (ω ∈ (0, ∞).) ω > 0: the open unit ball of Euclid n is nonempty and open, and volume on Euclid n is an additive Haar measure, hence positive on nonempty open sets (Metric.measure_ball_pos). ω < ∞: Euclid n is a proper space and volume is finite on compact sets, so balls have finite measure (measure_ball_lt_top). (For n = 0, Euclid 0 is a point and ω = 1.)
2. (Evaluating ν on balls.) For every R ∈ ℝ the ball B_R(0) is open, hence measurable (measurableSet_ball). By the hypothesis on ν, Measure.sum_apply, Measure.smul_apply and Measure.restrict_apply: ν(B_R(0)) = Σ'_{z∈Z} a(z)·Hⁿ(B_R(0) ∩ Π_z) = Σ'_{z∈Z} a(z)·Hⁿ(Π_z ∩ B_R(0)).
3. (Reduction to finite partial sums.) Every family in [0, ∞] is summable, and its sum is ≤ 1 as soon as every finite partial sum is ≤ 1 (ENNReal.summable.tsum_le_of_sum_le). So fix a finite set s of elements of the subtype Z and put S := Σ_{z∈s} a(z) ∈ [0, ∞]. It suffices to prove S ≤ 1.
4. (A common bound for the offsets.) Put M := Σ_{z∈s}‖z‖ ≥ 0. Then ‖z‖ ≤ M for every z ∈ s (one nonnegative term is at most the finite sum of nonnegative terms, Finset.single_le_sum).
5. (Key inequality.) Let R > M; then R > 0. We show S·ofReal((R − M)ⁿ) ≤ ofReal(Rⁿ).
 (a) A finite partial sum of nonnegative terms is at most the full sum (ENNReal.sum_le_tsum); with step 2 and the growth hypothesis at R > 0: Σ_{z∈s} a(z)·Hⁿ(Π_z ∩ B_R(0)) ≤ Σ'_{z∈Z} a(z)·Hⁿ(Π_z ∩ B_R(0)) = ν(B_R(0)) ≤ ω·ofReal(Rⁿ).
 (b) Let z ∈ s. Then z ∈ Z ⊆ V^⊥ and ‖z‖ ≤ M < R, so plane_ball gives Hⁿ(Π_z ∩ B_R(0)) = ω·ofReal((√(R² − ‖z‖²))ⁿ). Moreover 0 < R − M ≤ √(R² − ‖z‖²): since 0 ≤ ‖z‖ ≤ M we have ‖z‖² ≤ M², hence R² − ‖z‖² − (R − M)² = 2RM − M² − ‖z‖² ≥ 2RM − 2M² = 2M(R − M) ≥ 0, i.e. (R − M)² ≤ R² − ‖z‖², and Real.le_sqrt_of_sq_le gives R − M ≤ √(R² − ‖z‖²). As t ↦ tⁿ is monotone on [0, ∞) and ofReal and multiplication by ω are monotone, ω·ofReal((R − M)ⁿ) ≤ Hⁿ(Π_z ∩ B_R(0)).
 (c) Distributing the finite sum (Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum, commutativity in [0, ∞]) and using (b) termwise, then (a): ω·(S·ofReal((R − M)ⁿ)) = Σ_{z∈s} a(z)·(ω·ofReal((R − M)ⁿ)) ≤ Σ_{z∈s} a(z)·Hⁿ(Π_z ∩ B_R(0)) ≤ ω·ofReal(Rⁿ).
 (d) Since ω ≠ 0 and ω ≠ ∞ (step 1), ω may be cancelled (ENNReal.mul_le_mul_iff_right): S·ofReal((R − M)ⁿ) ≤ ofReal(Rⁿ).
6. (Dividing.) For R > M, (R − M)ⁿ > 0, so ofReal((R − M)ⁿ) is neither 0 nor ∞, and step 5 is equivalent (ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le) to S ≤ ofReal(Rⁿ)/ofReal((R − M)ⁿ) = ofReal(Rⁿ/(R − M)ⁿ) (ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos) = ofReal((R/(R − M))ⁿ) (div_pow).
7. (Letting R → ∞.) As R → ∞, R − M → ∞, so M/(R − M) → 0 (Tendsto.div_atTop) and 1 + M/(R − M) → 1. For R > M, R/(R − M) = 1 + M/(R − M); hence R/(R − M) → 1, (R/(R − M))ⁿ → 1 (continuity of t ↦ tⁿ) and ofReal((R/(R − M))ⁿ) → ofReal(1) = 1 (ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal). By step 6, S ≤ ofReal((R/(R − M))ⁿ) for every R > M, i.e. eventually as R → ∞, so S ≤ 1 (ge_of_tendsto, [0, ∞] being order-closed). (This is the selected proof's ε-argument made explicit: (√(R² − ‖z‖²)/R)ⁿ ≥ (1 − M/R)ⁿ, which tends to 1.)
8. (Conclusion.) Every finite partial sum of a over Z is ≤ 1, so by step 3, Σ'_{w∈Z} a(w) ≤ 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: ω_n ∈ (0, ∞), and ν(B_R(0)) = Σ'_{z∈Z} a(z)·Hⁿ({y : y − z ∈ V} ∩ B_R(0)) for every R.
It suffices to bound every finite partial sum S = Σ_{z∈s} a(z); let M := Σ_{z∈s}‖z‖ bound the offsets in s.
For R > M, plane_ball and √(R² − ‖z‖²) ≥ R − M give ω_n·S·ofReal((R − M)ⁿ) ≤ ν(B_R(0)) ≤ ω_n·ofReal(Rⁿ); cancelling ω_n and dividing, S ≤ ofReal((R/(R − M))ⁿ).
Since (R/(R − M))ⁿ → 1 as R → ∞, S ≤ 1, hence Σ'_{w∈Z} a(w) ≤ 1.

audit.reason: The proof establishes the exact unconditional ENNReal sum bound. Measurable-ball evaluation permits arbitrary Z. For each finite partial sum, the common offset bound gives the stated inequality; cancellation and division use explicitly positive finite factors. The limit at infinity and finite-partial-sum criterion complete the argument, including n = 0 and potentially infinite weights. Only plane_ball is needed.
